canonical_title: Risk: gating Product Mission acceleration on a governance mission's own closure is deliberate, but it depends on the same still-manual OLE trigger already flagged as a gap
summary: SB-P-1.12 is explicitly held not-activated until SB-GOV-IV-1.0 satisfies the standing OLE learning handoff or an explicit no-material-learning disposition, and communication is closed/archived -- a deliberate sequencing control so the verification-governance capability is proven and reflected on before the product program that will depend on it accelerates. This sequencing control itself depends on a human or builder manually initiating the OLE learning handoff, the same manual-trigger dependency already identified as an unresolved risk in SB-ORG-LEARNING-1.1 (Stage 4B, GitHub Issue #590) and not yet removed.

claims.text: The activation record explicitly states that before SB-P-1.12 may start: this activation record must be merged and verified on canonical main; SB-GOV-IV-1.0 must satisfy the standing OLE learning handoff or explicit evidence-based no-reusable-learning rule; communication must be closed/archived according to protocol; and Mission Control must then separately activate SB-P-1.12.

evidence.locator: Section 5, 'Product Mission boundary': 'This activation does not activate SB-P-1.12. Before SB-P-1.12 may start: 1. this activation record must be merged and verified on canonical main; 2. SB-GOV-IV-1.0 must satisfy the standing OLE learning handoff or explicit evidence-based no-reusable-learning rule; 3. communication must be closed/archived according to protocol; 4. Mission Control must then separately activate SB-P-1.12.'

claims.text: Mission Control's own post-activation verification record explicitly frames this handoff as manual specifically because Stage 4B background automation remains deferred, and directs the learning operator to work only from canonical merged evidence -- the same human-initiation dependency previously observed and retained as an unresolved risk in SB-ORG-LEARNING-1.1's own learning cycle recurred here, in the very next mission to close.

evidence.locator: Section 3, 'Manual OLE handoff scope': 'Stage 4B remains deferred, so this learning cycle is manual. The learning operator shall work only from canonical merged evidence and the accepted OLE v1 contracts.'

claims.text: The standing Mission Control closure rule (requiring an OLE learning handoff or an explicit no-material-reusable-learning disposition before a mission is considered closed) was applied to SB-GOV-IV-1.0 exactly as written, confirming the rule generalized beyond the organizational-learning mission that first established it rather than being scoped only to its own closure.

evidence.locator: Section 2, 'Standing OLE closure rule': 'The standing Mission Control closure rule requires every mission to complete either: 1. an OLE learning handoff; or 2. an explicit evidence-based NO MATERIAL REUSABLE LEARNING disposition.'

conditions: Applies when a governance- or capability-building mission's completion is a prerequisite for accelerating a larger program, and the organization wants that prerequisite genuinely proven and reflected on, not merely declared done.

The manual-trigger observation applies specifically while Stage 4B (or equivalent background automation) remains unimplemented; every mission closure in that state will keep depending on a human or builder remembering to initiate the learning cycle.
anti_patterns: Treating a governance/verification-capability mission's activation as equivalent to its closure, and starting dependent product work before the standing closure rule (learning handoff or explicit no-learning disposition) is actually satisfied.

Assuming the standing closure rule's manual-trigger dependency was a one-off characteristic of the mission that first defined it, rather than a still-open, generally-applicable gap that will recur at every mission closure until Stage 4B automation exists.
